{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.",
    "If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33), model often underestimates; adjust downward bias by 5–10% relative to recent mean.",
    "After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior peak), model frequently overshoots; apply a 1–2 day lag correction or reduce forecast slope.",
    "When true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 80), model often fails to recognize it; reduce forecast by 2–5% from recent peak.",
    "If sentiment shifts from positive to negative within 3–5 days, model often fails to adjust; trigger a downward correction if sentiment drops below 0.33.",
    "For 30-day forecasts, if model shows linear upward trend with no volatility, true outcome often exhibits volatility or sharp drop; add volatility buffer or adjust for regime change.",
    "If sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67) and price is near 80–85, model often overcorrects; cap forecast at 85–86 and reduce slope for next 3 days."
  ]
}
